confidence.method: score = 100 x (1 - 3/n) x r, where n is the number of valid inputs that gave identical output (rule of three) and r is 1.0 if every claim was demonstrated on the original (the exploit worked on it, the incident input broke it), else 0.7. 0 if any valid input changed, the fix is still exploitable or it still fails on the incident input. A heuristic, not a probability.

categories.csv-structure: a comma inside a quoted CSV field
categories.delimiter-mix: values that combine another delimiter character (; tab |) with quotes, written quoted and unquoted; reviewed instead of failed when shell-metachar or quotes is under review
categories.duplicate: a value copied from another row (duplicate keys)
categories.file-structure: the sample itself, a header-only file, and CRLF line endings
categories.flip: a true/false value set to the other value (or set where the sample has none)
categories.null-column: every value in one column empty (NULL once loaded into SQL)
categories.numeric-format: integers, decimals, signs, exponents, underscores, leading zeros, rounding edges
